learning_outcomes.text: Understands how the length of the investment realization period and the distribution of investment outlays over time affect the total costs of its realization.
Knows what the individual components of annual costs in power engineering represent, knows the basic relationships allowing for their calculation.

Knows what the impact of load variability over time on the costs of electricity generation, transmission, and distribution entails, knows the basic relationships for calculating power and energy losses in network elements.
Knows what the methods for comparing and evaluating the economic efficiency of investments are, knows the basic relationships used in these methods.
Knows the legal basis for settlements for electricity transmission and distribution, knows what the individual components of transmission and distribution charges represent.
Is able to perform calculations of electricity generation and transmission costs, can analyze the obtained results.
Is able to apply in practice the learned methods for evaluating and comparing different investment variants in power engineering from an economic perspective.
Is able to describe and present calculation and analysis results.
Is able to cooperate in a group to achieve common tasks.
Knows how electricity generation affects the natural environment, understands the need for rational energy use.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to economic calculation functions in spreadsheets and their use for: calculating electricity generation and transmission costs, evaluating the efficiency of power investments, and calculating electricity supply costs for consumers.

Designing and economically comparing two variants of power supply for an industrial facility. The project includes choosing the supply voltage, selecting devices, calculating investment outlays, operating costs, choosing a tariff, and calculating energy supply costs.
Energy resources. The impact of electricity production on the environment (2 h)
Economic issues in the power system (2 h).
Investment processes in power engineering (2 h).
Cost accounting in power engineering – fixed costs, variable costs, reliability costs, environmental usage costs (2 h).
Load variability and its impact on the operating costs of the power system (2 h).
Power and energy losses in power grids, methods for calculating losses (2 h).
Technical and economic aspects of reactive power generation and transmission in the power system (2 h).
Investment and non-investment methods for limiting power and energy losses in power grids (2 h).
Static methods for evaluating the efficiency of power investments (2 h).
Dynamic methods for evaluating the efficiency of power investments (2 h).
Legal basis for the energy market and settlements for electricity and transmission services (2 h).
Electricity tariffs and transmission and distribution services (2 h).
Selected optimization issues in power engineering (4 h).
assessment_rules: Lectures, laboratory classes, and project classes will have their learning outcomes verified through various methods including project execution, laboratory class execution, examination, test results, and completion of laboratory classes. For laboratory classes, students must be prepared for the exercise, which may be verified by an oral or written colloquium. Completion of laboratory classes requires presenting a solution to the problem. Completion of the module depends on completing all laboratory classes. For project classes, the method of project execution and the final outcome are evaluated.
